# 4. Harness layer: how you run, test and trust it

[← Home](../README.md) · [The stack](README.md) · [Data layer](data.md) · [Agent layer](agent.md) · [Execution layer](execution.md) · **Harness layer** · [Application layer](application.md)

> **Is the result real, and would we notice if it stopped being real?**

**Scope.** Research and backtest environments, simulators and paper-trading gyms, benchmarks and live arenas, robustness and bias control, and the agent harness itself: loops, evals, traces and durable state.

**Where it usually breaks:** a test window the model has already read (look-ahead); headline Sharpe ratios from a few months; costs and slippage left out; regressions found in production instead of in a replayed trace.

**Open gap.** No catalogued agentic system's headline trading table can be regenerated from its repository. Live arenas fix look-ahead but run for weeks, far too short to separate skill from luck.

20 repos · 30 papers · 16 articles and posts. Legend: 🟢 active · 🟡 slowing · ⚪ dormant (last commit within 90 days, within a year, or older, counted from the check date) · 💤 declared unmaintained · ⚡ can place real orders · 📝 paper trading only · 🧩 open core with proprietary parts · 🔒 source-available, restricted · ❓ license unclear · 🧰 general-purpose tool applied here · 📖 read in full · 🗂️ machine-extracted [method card](../docs/cards/index.md) · 🔖 abstract only. Marks on a row link to the lines that support them, at the commit we checked.

## Also relevant from other layers

Listed in their primary layer; they also ship working code for this one.

- [Claude Trading Skills](https://github.com/tradermonty/claude-trading-skills) — Claude Skills for market-regime checks, screening, position sizing, journaling and backtest review. *Primary: [Application layer](application.md).*
- [FinRL](https://github.com/AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRL) — Deep reinforcement learning library and tutorials for stock trading environments. *Primary: [Agent layer](agent.md).*
- [FinRL-X (FinRL-Trading)](https://github.com/AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRL-Trading) — Weight-centric pipeline that backtests target weights and sends them to a broker. *Primary: [Execution layer](execution.md).*
- [Kalshi AI Trading Bot](https://github.com/ryanfrigo/kalshi-ai-trading-bot) — Kalshi trading toolkit with an edge audit, MCP server and agent tools. *Primary: [Application layer](application.md).*
- [Kraken CLI](https://github.com/krakenfx/kraken-cli) — Kraken's CLI and MCP server: live orders, funding and a built-in paper engine at live prices. *Primary: [Execution layer](execution.md).*
- [LEAN](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean) — Event-driven algorithmic trading engine for research, backtesting and live trading. *Primary: [Execution layer](execution.md).*
- [NautilusTrader](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader) — Event-driven engine running the same strategy code in backtest and live. *Primary: [Execution layer](execution.md).*
- [QuantDinger](https://github.com/OpenByteInc/QuantDinger) — Self-hosted AI research, backtest and live-trading backend with an agent gateway and MCP server. *Primary: [Application layer](application.md).*
- [Qwen DianJin](https://github.com/aliyun/qwen-dianjin) — Alibaba Cloud hub for finance reasoning models, datasets and benchmarks. *Primary: [Agent layer](agent.md).*
- [TradingView MCP (screener and data)](https://github.com/atilaahmettaner/tradingview-mcp) — Headless MCP server for screeners, indicator reads and simple backtests, no TradingView account needed. *Primary: [Data layer](data.md).*
- [Vibe-Trading](https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading) — Personal trading-agent stack (CLI, MCP, web): research, backtests with run cards and validation, paper accounts and a reconciling live runner. *Primary: [Application layer](application.md).*

## Papers

### Research and backtest environments

| Paper | Authors, year | Read | Takeaway |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Hard to Fool: A Bounded LLM Research Loop for Quantitative Finance, and What Two Dozen Campaigns Found](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06607) | Henry Zhang, 2026 | 🔖 abstract | Autonomous Quant Researcher: an open-source research loop where the model proposes strict declarative JSON over a fixed vocabulary and only trusted code decides, with chronological discovery, validation and a holdout that can be opened once, absolute acceptance gates and a hash-chained append-only ledger. Reports every campaign run to date. Limit: Most hypotheses fail; a language-model survivor that passed discovery and validation with Sharpe ratios near 3 fell to 0.26 on its single holdout use. |

| [What LLM Trading Agents Actually Do in Production: A Six-Month, Population-Scale Record from Two Fleets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05663) | T. J. Barton et al., 2026 | 🔖 abstract | Operator-reported record of real-money LLM agents in two fleets run by the authors, in separate windows: about 3,500 user-funded vaults trading Base memecoins for 21 days, and 500 to 600 user-created agents on Hyperliquid perpetuals from June to August 2026. The abstract reports that platform controls shaped behaviour more than strategy text and that neither fleet showed a directional edge, with the perpetuals fleet unprofitable and behind a matched retail benchmark. |
| [Can AI Make Money in Crypto? Measuring the Gap from Backtests to Real Markets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34510) | Xingtong Yu et al., 2026 | 🔖 abstract | Unified benchmark that runs machine-learning, reinforcement-learning, LLM and agent trading methods in crypto markets through three stages: historical backtest, prospective exchange paper trading and real-money live trading, to quantify the backtest-to-realization gap. Ships an open-source system and a continuously updated public platform. Limit: The abstract reports no numbers: gap sizes, live capital and live window length are not stated there, so the strength of the real-money evidence must be checked in the paper. |
| [MintEval: Do LLMs Implement the Trading Strategy You Asked For? A Behavioural-Equivalence Benchmark for Natural-Language-to-Strategy Code](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03080) | Siyu Wang et al., 2026 | 🔖 abstract | MintEval: 800 tasks on BTCUSDT 15-minute data where a model re-implements a programmatically generated reference strategy from colloquial trader instructions; generated and reference programs are compared bar by bar on actions, not on profit or code similarity. Limit: A frontier model still fails silently on 0.275 of tasks, and an LLM judge from a recent strategy-generation benchmark accepted every one of the silent failures. |
| [LLM Trading Agents Earn Beta, Not Alpha: A Look-Ahead-Free Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19530) | Jackson Wang, 2026 | 🔖 abstract | rta-bench-1: a backtest over three US market regimes that shows each headline only after its publication minute and splits returns into factor exposure and alpha. In 91 runs of six models from four vendors, no alpha was significant. Limit: Market and style exposure accounted for a median 78% of return, and decisions did no better than random stocks of the same sector; two same-model runs differing only in seed ended 5.2 points apart on average. |

### Robustness and bias control

| Paper | Authors, year | Read | Takeaway |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Assessing Look-Ahead Bias in Stock Return Predictions Generated By GPT Sentiment Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17322) | Paul Glasserman et al., 2023 | 🔖 abstract | Shows that GPT sentiment backtests on news from inside the model's training period are contaminated by look-ahead and by a distraction effect from general knowledge of the company. |
| ⭐ [Can LLM-based Financial Investing Strategies Outperform the Market in Long Run?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07078) | Weixian Waylon Li et al., 2025 | 📖 partial | FINSABER: bias-aware backtester (survivorship, look-ahead, data snooping) run over two decades and 100+ symbols; earlier LLM advantages shrink. |
| [TradeTrap: Are LLM-based Trading Agents Truly Reliable and Faithful?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02261) | Lewen Yan et al., 2025 | 🗂️ [card](../docs/cards/2512.02261.md) | TradeTrap: stress tests four agent components (market intelligence, strategy, ledger, execution) with injected faults and attacks. |
| [A Fast and Effective Solution to the Problem of Look-ahead Bias in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06607) | Humzah Merchant et al., 2025 | 🗂️ [card](../docs/cards/2512.06607.md) | Inference-time logit adjustment with two small models (one tuned on information to forget, one on information to keep) to mimic an earlier knowledge cutoff. |
| ⭐ [Detecting Lookahead Bias in LLM Forecasts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23847) | Zhenyu Gao et al., 2025 | 🗂️ [card](../docs/cards/2512.23847.md) | Lookahead Propensity (LAP): date-only recall query that estimates how much an LLM has memorized an outcome; used to test forecast contamination. |
| [Adversarial News and Lost Profits: Manipulating Headlines in LLM-Driven Algorithmic Trading](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13082) | Advije Rizvani et al., 2026 | 🗂️ [card](../docs/cards/2601.13082.md) | Human-imperceptible headline manipulations (homoglyphs, hidden text) mislead LLM sentiment inside a backtested trader, cutting annual returns by up to 17.7 percentage points. |
| [What survives honest evaluation? Leakage-safe, search-aware assessment of LLM-driven trading strategy discovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27734) | Eray Gençay, 2026 | 🔖 abstract | Strategy-discovery system in which the agent acts only through registry-validated tools that exclude look-ahead by construction, and every evaluation is counted so reported performance is deflated by the trial count. Tested on a 453-stock point-in-time US universe and 39 ETFs with transaction, impact and borrow costs. Limit: Honest evaluation rejected every LLM-discovered strategy; a deliberately leaky oracle with a Sharpe ratio of 35 passed Deflated Sharpe and PBO tests, so statistical correction does not replace a look-ahead guard. |
| [Trading Agents or Market Crashers? Dissecting Robustness and Security Failures in Academic Financial LLM Trading Schemes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19705) | Mengxiao Wang et al., 2026 | 🔖 abstract | FARSIGHT: a systematization that rates 15 academic LLM trading schemes on robustness to market stress and on security against source manipulation and agent compromise, checking the ratings against the 7 released codebases, then simulates markets driven by the agents' decisions. Limit: No paper describes a halt that skips LLM inference, and the 7 code releases enforce no stop-loss or position limit outside the LLM; the market-crash results come from a simulation with 400 agents. |
| [Fake News, Real Crashes: Information Injection Attacks on LLM Financial Trading Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26438) | Mengxiao Wang et al., 2026 | 🔖 abstract | Attack benchmark for information injection against LLM trading agents: five injection vectors and seven event categories over about 10,000 decisions on 15 US stocks. Prompt injection reached 14% attack success while fabricated news reached 62%. Limit: Most attacks evade standard defenses: model scaling stops shallow vectors but not fact poisoning, peer debate fails, and only hierarchical aggregation reduces attack success. |
| [Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03985) | Amir Dehkordi et al., 2026 | 🔖 abstract | OLIVIA: a test protocol with point-in-time inputs, masked company identities, validation-only selection, a hash-frozen analysis plan and a test period unblinded once. Applied to a fine-tuned open-weights decision model and three commercial models reading S&P 500 news. Limit: The fine-tuned model's daily IC fell from 0.055 and 0.065 on validation to 0.020 on the blinded January to July 2026 test; no pre-registered strategy survives costs and a deflated Sharpe ratio, and commercial models identified masked companies in 62% to 74% of cases. |
| [Short Windows, Unmodelled Costs, Unknown Cutoffs: A Pre-Registered Evidence Audit of 91 LLM Trading Papers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18934) | Henry Zhang, 2026 | 🔖 abstract | Pre-registered audit of 91 LLM trading and alpha-mining papers against a ten-field rubric, with every code backed by a script-checked verbatim quote. Of 75 papers with a trading test, 51% deduct no costs and the median test window is 12 months. Limit: Three of five pre-registered hypotheses failed: links between headline Sharpe and window length or costs were not detectable in the 13 papers that state a headline Sharpe. |
| [The Only Edge Was Memorized in Training: LLM Trading Agents Around Earnings and Bad News](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22177) | Jackson Wang, 2026 | 🔖 abstract | Tests LLM agents before 598 earnings announcements and after 409 bad-news drops of large US stocks on a look-ahead-free benchmark, comparing staged agents with single calls, simple rules and a logistic regression, with and without the stock's name. Limit: Across five models from four vendors no agent beat the simple bets; given only ticker and dates, a GPT-based model called direction on 59.2% of announcements before its training cutoff and 53.3% after it. |

### Agent harness: loops, evals, traces and state

| Paper | Authors, year | Read | Takeaway |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AllPath: Layered Verification for a Deployed, Self-Revising LLM Trading Agent under Human-Gated and Autonomous Regimes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26662) | Tian Zhang et al., 2026 | 🔖 abstract | AllPath: report on a personal LLM trading agent deployed against a live paper-brokerage account that reviews its own day nightly and proposes strategy revisions, verified in three layers (deterministic code gates, bounded self-review, human approval). Compares two and a half weeks of human-gated self-revision with five weeks of auto-applied revisions. Limit: The code gates rejected no proposal, the human later removed 11 of the 19 rules the agent had added on its own, and the most instructive incidents passed every gate and were found by hand. |

## Articles and posts

Newest first. Icons: 𝕏 post · 📝 blog · 📘 docs · 📰 news · 🎧 podcast · 🎤 talk · 📄 paper or report. A post is listed for the idea it carries; its own performance claims are not verified here. Undated pages show the date we checked them.

- 📘 [Task verifiers](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/verifier) — Harbor Framework, undated (checked 2026-10-26). How a container task's verifier runs after the agent finishes and writes a reward. A clean template for grading trading-agent tasks (build a backtest, reconcile a book) independently of the agent.
- 📘 [LangGraph persistence: checkpointers and stores](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/persistence) — LangChain, undated (checked 2026-10-26). Thread checkpoints give resume, human-in-the-loop approval and time travel; stores give cross-run memory. TradingAgents and several projects here are built on LangGraph.
- 📘 [Strategies (Pine Script v6 user manual)](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/strategies/) — TradingView, undated (checked 2026-10-26). The broker emulator's own realism caveats: intrabar paths inferred from OHLC unless the bar magnifier is on, unrealistic results on synthetic charts, and caps on bars and trades. Check these before trusting an agent-generated Pine backtest.
- 📝 [Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop](https://claude.com/resources/articles/building-agents-when-to-fold-subagents-into-your-main-agent-loop) — Diane Sarkis (Anthropic), 2026-10-22. Many agents do better as one loop with skills loaded on demand than as a coordinator with many subagents. Keep subagents for context isolation, parallel independent work or conflicting instructions, and migrate under evals. Directly relevant to analyst/risk/trader agent teams.
- 📘 [AI in financial services: good practice and areas for improvement](https://www.fca.org.uk/publications/good-poor-practice/ai-financial-services) — Financial Conduct Authority, 2026-10-19. UK regulator's examples of good and poor practice for machine learning, generative and agentic AI. Useful as a control checklist: a central inventory of agents with owner, access and controls, and logs of prompts, outputs, model versions and escalations. It creates no new requirements.
- 📝 [Pi Durable](https://earendil.com/posts/pi-durable/) — Earendil Engineering, 2026-10-01. Every step of an agent run is a checkpointed task, so a new process can resume after a crash. Read alongside the execution rule: replaying a step is not the same as knowing whether its order reached the broker.
- 📝 [Toward Recursive Self-Improvement: How GLM Built Its Own Inference Infrastructure](https://z.ai/blog/glm-built-its-inference-infrastructure) — Z.ai, 2026-09-17. A company's account of an infrastructure agent driven by dense, verifiable feedback, with objectives and risk kept by people. The lesson transfers: verifiable feedback loops, not credit for every gain to the agent. Claims are the company's own.
- 📄 [Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14858) — Tong Zheng et al., 2026-09-14. Improves an agent's exploration policy offline by replaying its stored discovery history. An idea for budgeting strategy search; any trading use needs a held-out set that the improvement loop never sees.
- 📄 [Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents (a source-code study of eleven systems)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00006) — Paul Barbaste et al., 2026-07-15 (arXiv lists v1 as submitted 2026-07-15 although the identifier is in the 2609 series). Maps seven subsystems and 29 design patterns across eleven coding-agent harnesses. A vocabulary for the harness around a trading agent; it is a study of coding agents, not a capability table for trading.
- 📝 [Your LLM's Alpha Might Be Mere Memorization](https://hedgefundalpha.com/education/your-llms-alpha-might-be-mere-memorization/) — Greg Kapoustin (Hedge Fund Alpha), 2026-04-21. Practitioner essay: LLM backtest edges often vanish after the training cutoff, so point-in-time integrity has to cover the model as well as the data.
- 📝 [Harness design for long-running application development](https://www.anthropic.com/research/harness-design-long-running-apps) — Prithvi Rajasekaran (Anthropic), 2026-03-24. Separate the generator from a skeptical evaluator, and revisit the harness with every new model to drop scaffolding it no longer needs. The case for an independent verifier, in practice.
- 📘 [2026 FINRA Annual Regulatory Oversight Report: GenAI and AI agents](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/guidance/reports/2026-finra-annual-regulatory-oversight-report/gen-ai) — FINRA, 2025-12-09. A US regulator's list of AI-agent risks broker-dealers must supervise: autonomy, scope and authority, auditability, data sensitivity, reward misalignment. A checklist for any harness that lets an agent act.
- 📝 [Effective harnesses for long-running agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents) — Justin Young (Anthropic), 2025-11-26. An initializer agent sets up the scaffolding; a worker agent does one unit per session, tests end to end, and leaves git history and progress notes for the next session. The same pattern fits multi-day research and strategy builds.
- 𝕏 [Season 1.5 of Alpha Arena is live with $320K deployed](https://x.com/jay_azhang/status/1991256354657366251) — Jay A. Zhang (@jay_azhang, Nof1), 2025-11-19. The second season moved to US equities with several competition modes, framed as testing judgement rather than knowledge.
- 𝕏 [Season 1 of Alpha Arena has officially ended](https://x.com/jay_azhang/status/1985481491078328621) — Jay A. Zhang (@jay_azhang, Nof1), 2025-11-03. Results post that names the design limits shaping the outcome: numeric time-series-only context, a narrow asset universe, a limited action space, persistent model "personalities". Two weeks of one run cannot separate skill from luck.
- 𝕏 [Alpha Arena is live](https://x.com/jay_azhang/status/1979312946154033227) — Jay A. Zhang (@jay_azhang, Nof1), 2025-10-17. Launch of the first widely watched live, real-money benchmark of LLM traders: six models, $10K each, fully autonomous, crypto perpetuals.

## Builder notes

Recommendations from this list's maintainers, distilled from the sources above. They are design advice, not results reported by those sources.

- **Keep the verifier independent.** The component that grades a run must not share the agent's context or prompts. Fix the task, inputs, model and budget per experiment, turn every failed trace into a regression case, and keep a held-out set that no automatic improvement loop ever sees.
- **Write a run manifest for every backtest.** Record data snapshot, code commit, model and parameters, costs, and the in-sample and out-of-sample windows, and report results after costs. Use the [report card](../tools/evalkit/report_card.py) and the error bars in [reading a backtest](../docs/06-reading-a-backtest.md).
- **Prove a P&L with a ledger, not a screenshot.** A credible record shows when each input was available, the price it could have traded at, fees, realized and unrealized P&L, and drawdown. Screenshots of returns without an account ledger are marketing, however large the number.
